messages:
maya: Heads-up — reframe sprint for the battlecard vs cloud infra + LLM APIs. Need razor-sharp hooks for webinar, a 1-pager for field, and inbound routing snippets for SDRs. Can we run quick claim triage?
omar: +1. What's the highest friction claim we want to knock out first? latency vs cost vs reliability?
liam: Latency + graceful degradation sells well. Cloud vendors tout scale but dodge predictable latency at tail percentiles.
jess: Also call out rollout/compatibility friction vs self-hosted infra vendors — ops cost and versioning nightmares. Keep it simple for SDRs though.
maya: Agree. Draft plan: 1) Core claim matrix (what opponent says vs our counter) 2) Bench narrative (head-to-head latency profiles + cost per 1M tokens) 3) Webinar hook (customer story + live demo of failover).
anna-sdr: Need 3 quick rebut lines for SDRs — should be <20 words each. Also routing: which leads get the latency play vs cost play?
liam: Suggestion: route enterprise infra and infra-eval leads to latency/degradation play. Small SaaS to cost story. Use event tags: "latency-eval", "cost-eval".
maya: Good. I'll sketch soundbites. Posting initial one-liners: 
--
"Stop guessing on tail latency — predictable SLOs, guaranteed fallbacks"
"Cut inference spend with batching + KV caching — avoid oversized fleets"
"Same API across hosted/dedicated/private — one config, many runtimes"
--
jess: Love the 2nd one. Can we add a short line for security/compliance audience?
maya: Add: "Private deployments with KMS/HSM + audit trails — enterprise-ready."
omar: For bench narrative: we need reproducible test plan. Call out seq length, batch size, and model variants. Don't show cherry-picked numbers.
liam: I'll draft a minimal benchmark spec: 99th percentile latency for 1k concurrent requests, payload 256 tokens, model X vs model Y, + cost table. Quick sample: ```
bench.yaml
seq_len: 256
concurrency: 1000
metric: p99_latency_ms
models: [redwood-llm-v1, cloud-llm-2, open-quantized]
```
jess: Tagging comp-bot for a scan of public competitor claims. @comp-bot can you pull recent marketing claims about "scale" and "zero-config managed endpoints"?
comp-bot: (automated) Pulled 12 recent claims from CloudVendorA and APIVendorB. Highlights saved to https://wiki.redwood.ai/comp-summaries/1754449000
maya: Nice. For webinar: propose 20-min product + 10-min customer + 15-min live failover demo. Live demo should show automatic fallback to smaller quantized model when capacity hits threshold.
anna-sdr: That demo sounds gold for SDR outreach. Can we capture a 30-sec clip for prospecting sequences?
liam: Yep. I'll script a 30-sec clip: "Redwood maintains sub-200ms p99 under 2x load by routing to optimized quantized variants — no code changes."
maya: Tactical asks: Liam -> benchmark spec + clip script by EOD tomorrow. Jess -> one-pager for field with 3 rebut lines and routing rules. Omar -> update inbound routing playbook to add tags and lead scoring adjustments. Anna -> quick SDR blurbs and suggested sequences.
omar: On it. Small question: do we surface cost numbers in public one-pager or keep them field-only?
jess: Field-only. Public can be % savings ranges without absolute $s.
maya: Agreed. Keep exact numbers gated. Also: create a "quick claims vs clouds" table with 2 columns: Opponent claim / Redwood counter. Short bullets only.
liam: I'll populate initial table in the draft doc. Link for review: https://docs.redwood.ai/market/battlecard-reshuffle-draft (internal).
anna-sdr: When should SDRs expect the update? We want to swap new snippets into sequences before next webinar (Friday).
maya: Target: swap on Thursday morning. Reviews close Wednesday 5pm.
comp-bot: (automated) Noting deadline: 1754535400 for review close.
omar: tiny nit: can we avoid the word "managed" when describing opponents — it's ambiguous. Use "opaque managed endpoints" or "proprietary managed endpoints".
jess: Good call. Also include 2 customer quotes for the one-pager: one on latency, one on cost predictability. I'll source from case studies.
maya: Perfect. Final ask: reactions and short approvals here. If no objections, I'll lock the draft and kick off the design ticket. :sparkles:
liam: :thumbsup:
anna-sdr: :raised_hands:
jess: :white_check_mark:
omar: :+1:
maya: Thanks team — I'll post the draft thread shortly and tag for reviews.
